definition_zh: 尝试；努力；试用；审判
definition_en: to make an effort to do something, or to test something to see whether it works
core_image: 一个人踮起脚去够高架子最上层的那只盒子
scene: 厨房的吊柜太高，个子矮的人伸手够不着最里面那只盒子。She tried again and again until her fingers touched the box.
sceneCN: 这里 try 是「尝试；努力」（第 1 个义项：付出力气去做一件不容易做到的事）；句意为她一次又一次地试，直到手指碰到那只盒子。踮脚去够高处盒子的动作，就是这个词的样子。

derivatives.zh: 由 try 同源的 trial 构成，义为「试验；审判」
由 try 加 -ing 构成，义为「难熬的；考验人的」
由 try 加 -er 构成，义为「努力尝试的人」

senses.title: The reaching hand
senses.definition: to make an effort to do something difficult
senses.definitionCN: 付出力气去做一件不容易做到的事
senses.example: She tried to lift the box but it was too heavy.
senses.exampleCN: 她试着抬起那只箱子，但它太重了。
senses.why: The core of the word is effort spent on something that may fail.
senses.whyCN: 这个词的核心是把力气花在一件可能失败的事情上。

senses.title: The small test
senses.definition: to use or do something briefly in order to find out whether it is good
senses.definitionCN: 短暂地使用或做某事，以判断它是否合适
senses.example: Try this soup and tell me if it needs more salt.
senses.exampleCN: 尝尝这汤，告诉我是不是还要加点盐。
senses.why: Testing is effort made cheap: you risk little and learn a lot.
senses.whyCN: 试用的本质是廉价的努力：冒很小的风险，换回很多信息。

senses.title: One go at it
senses.definition: an attempt, counted as one of several
senses.definitionCN: 作为若干次中的一次而努力
senses.example: It took him three tries before the door opened.
senses.exampleCN: 他试了三次，门才开。
senses.why: The verb turns into a countable noun, so attempts can be numbered.
senses.whyCN: 动词转成可数名词，于是尝试可以被数出来。

senses.title: The courtroom
senses.definition: to examine a case and decide whether someone is guilty
senses.definitionCN: 审理案件并裁定某人是否有罪
senses.example: The case will be tried in the county court next month.
senses.exampleCN: 此案将于下月在郡法院审理。
senses.why: A court also puts a case to the test, which is why the legal sense grew from the same idea.
senses.whyCN: 法庭同样是在对案件加以检验，法律义便由同一个观念长出。

intro.en: Try came into English from Old French trier, to sift or pick out, a word whose own origin is much debated.
intro.cn: try 来自古法语 trier（筛、挑选），而这个词本身的来源众说纷纭。

items.en: Trier meant to sift grain, separating the good from the bad.
items.cn: 古法语 trier 意为筛谷，把好的与坏的分开。

items.en: English borrowed it as trien, to examine or to sift a matter.
items.cn: 英语借入作 trien，意为审查或筛选一件事。

items.en: From examining a matter came the legal sense: to try a case in court.
items.cn: 由审查一件事生出法律义：在法庭上审理案件。

items.en: The everyday sense of attempting something grew out of the idea of putting it to the test.
items.cn: 日常的「尝试」义由「加以检验」这一观念发展而来。

items.en: Today try covers effort, experiment and trial at law, all bound by the act of testing.
items.cn: 今天 try 兼指努力、试验与审判，三者都由「检验」这一动作连在一起。

note.en: The first group collects words that look like try, the second collects closer meanings.
note.cn: 第一组收形近词，第二组收义近词。

entries.definition: A formal test or a court hearing.
A group of people who share ancestry.
Too common to be interesting.
To make an effort at something.
To work hard towards a goal.
To check how well something works.

normalIntro.en: Try is short and blunt: one syllable holding a whole handful of effort.
normalIntro.cn: try 短促干脆：一个音节里装了一整把力气。

normal.en: The y changes to i before -es and -ed: tries, tried.
normal.cn: 加 -es、-ed 时 y 变 i：tries、tried。

normal.en: Try takes a to-infinitive when it means effort: try to open it.
normal.cn: 表示努力时后接不定式：try to open it。

normal.en: Try plus a gerund means an experiment: try opening it.
normal.cn: 后接动名词则表示试验：try opening it。

normal.en: Trial and try come from the same French root.
normal.cn: trial 与 try 同出法语词根。

normal.en: The court sense keeps the old idea of testing a case.
normal.cn: 法庭义保留了检验案件的古老观念。

abstract.en: A hand stretched towards a shelf just out of reach.
abstract.cn: 一只伸向刚好够不着的架子的手。

abstract.en: A spoon lifted to the lips with a doubtful face.
abstract.cn: 一把迟疑地送到唇边的勺子。

abstract.en: Three chalk marks on a door frame, one for each failure.
abstract.cn: 门框上三道粉笔痕，一次失败一道。

examples.en: Try to keep your voice low in the library.
examples.cn: 在图书馆里尽量把声音压低。

examples.en: She tried the new keyboard and liked it at once.
examples.cn: 她试了新键盘，立刻就喜欢上了。

examples.en: After two failed tries he found the right key.
examples.cn: 失败了两次之后，他找到了对的那把钥匙。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「踹」——把门踹开得使劲，一次不行就再踹一次，就是努力尝试。

root: 源自中古英语 trien、古法语 trier（筛、挑），本义为把好坏分开、对事物加以检验，由此生出努力尝试、试用与法庭审判三义，同族词有 trial。

sensesIntro.en: From effort, through testing, to one counted attempt, and finally to the courtroom where a case is tested.
sensesIntro.cn: 从付出努力，到试用检验，再到可数的一次尝试，最后落到检验案件的法庭。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a hand reaching for a high shelf.
core.cn: 核心意象：伸向高处架子的手。

branches.en: The effort branch: the hand keeps reaching.
branches.cn: 努力分支：手一直往上够。

branches.en: The sample branch: a small taste before deciding.
branches.cn: 样品分支：先尝一口再决定。

branches.en: The count branch: attempts numbered like steps.
branches.cn: 计数分支：尝试像台阶一样被数出来。

branches.en: The test branch: effort shared by court and kitchen.
branches.cn: 检验分支：法庭与厨房共用同一份力气。

branches.en: The judgement branch: tasting and ruling both decide.
branches.cn: 判断分支：品尝与裁决都在做决定。

intro.en: Try is a free root of Romance origin, and the family grows with -al and -ing.
intro.cn: try 是源自罗曼语的自由词根，词族靠 -al、-ing 扩展。

latinIntro.en: The deeper source of the French verb is uncertain, so the list below stays close to the English family.
latinIntro.cn: 这个法语动词更深一层的来源尚无定论，因此下列条目限于英语词族本身。

items.meaning: he or she makes an effort
turns the stem into a noun

items.example: It also forms the adjective trying.

definition_zh: 转动；转弯；转变；轮到
definition_en: to move around a centre, to change direction, or to become something different
core_image: 门把手上的一只手轻轻一拧，门就开了
scene: 走廊尽头，探访者站在门前犹豫了一会儿。She turned the handle slowly and the door swung open.
sceneCN: 这里 turn 是「转动」（第 1 个义项：绕着一个中心旋转）；句意为她慢慢转动门把手，门就开了。手拧门把的那一下，就是这个词最本真的样子。

derivatives.zh: 由 turn 加 -ing 构成，义为「转弯处；转向」
由 turn 与 out 合成，义为「出席人数」
由 turn 加前缀 over 构成，义为「使翻倒；推翻」
由 turn 加前缀 re 构成，义为「返回」

senses.title: The handle
senses.definition: to move something round a fixed point
senses.definitionCN: 使某物绕着固定的一点旋转
senses.example: She turned the handle slowly and the door swung open.
senses.exampleCN: 她慢慢转动门把手，门就开了。
senses.why: The oldest sense is pure motion around a centre, with nothing else implied.
senses.whyCN: 最古老的含义就是绕中心旋转的纯动作，不带别的意味。

senses.title: The corner
senses.definition: to change the direction in which you face or move
senses.definitionCN: 改变朝向或行进的方向
senses.example: Turn right after the bridge and you will see the school.
senses.exampleCN: 过了桥向右转，你就能看见学校。
senses.why: Turning the body repeats the same motion on a larger scale.
senses.whyCN: 身体转向，不过是把同一个动作放大到整个人身上。

senses.title: The change of state
senses.definition: to become something else, often slowly
senses.definitionCN: 逐渐变成另一种样子
senses.example: The leaves turned yellow in a single cold week.
senses.exampleCN: 一场寒流过后，叶子一周就黄了。
senses.why: If a thing can turn, it can also turn into another shape, so the verb came to mean change.
senses.whyCN: 既然能转，就能转成另一副样子，于是这个动词获得了「改变」的意思。

senses.title: The rightful moment
senses.definition: the time when it is your chance to do something
senses.definitionCN: 该你做事的那一段时间
senses.example: It is your turn to choose the music.
senses.exampleCN: 轮到你选音乐了。
senses.why: Turns go round in a circle, back to each person in order.
senses.whyCN: 轮流本就是绕圈子来的，一圈后再回到每个人。

intro.en: Turn came from Old French torner, and behind it stands the Latin and Greek word for a lathe that spins wood.
intro.cn: turn 来自古法语 torner，再往上是拉丁语与希腊语中表示旋木车床的词。

items.en: Tornos named a lathe, a tool that spins wood against a blade.
items.cn: tornos 指车床，即让木料转着碰刀的工具。

items.en: Tornare took the meaning to turn, and the noun tornus named a circuit.
items.cn: tornare 取得「转」的含义，名词 tornus 指一圈。

items.en: Torner meant to turn, roll or change direction.
items.cn: torner 意为转、滚、改变方向。

items.en: Turne covered turning the body, turning a page, and turning into something.
items.cn: turne 涵盖转身、翻页和变成某物。

items.en: From the order of turns came the noun sense of a person's chance.
items.cn: 从轮转的次序生出名词义：一个人轮到的机会。

note.en: The first group shares the stem, the second collects other verbs of motion.
note.cn: 第一组共享词干，第二组收其他表示运动的动词。

entries.definition: To come back to a place.
A corner or a point of change.
Ripped apart.
To turn on an axis.
To turn quickly again and again.
To turn on a pivot.

normalIntro.en: Turn is the plain English word for going round, whether a handle, a head or a season.
normalIntro.cn: turn 是最朴素的「转」，门把、脑袋、季节都用它。

normal.en: Turn plus into means to become: water turns into ice.
normal.cn: 接 into 表示变成：water turns into ice。

normal.en: Turn on and turn off work for lights and machines.
normal.cn: 开关灯、开关机器用 turn on 和 turn off。

normal.en: Take turns comes from the round of a circle.
normal.cn: take turns 的轮流出自绕圈。

normal.en: The n is silent after the vowel in rapid speech, but not in writing.
normal.cn: 口语连读时 n 很轻，书写不可省。

normal.en: Return carries the same turning, only back.
normal.cn: return 带着同一个转，只是方向往回。

abstract.en: A palm pressing a brass handle down.
abstract.cn: 一只手掌把铜门把压下去。

abstract.en: A road bending out of sight behind a wall.
abstract.cn: 一条路在墙后拐出视野。

abstract.en: Leaves turning from green to gold.
abstract.cn: 叶子由绿转金。

examples.en: He turned the key twice before the lock gave way.
examples.cn: 他拧了两下钥匙，锁才开。

examples.en: Turn left at the fountain and follow the crowd.
examples.cn: 在喷泉处左转，跟着人群走。

examples.en: The wind turned cold the moment the sun went down.
examples.cn: 太阳一落，风就变冷了。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「腾」——一腾身就转过身去，转、转弯都是它。

root: 源自中古英语 turne、古法语 torner，再上溯拉丁语 tornare、希腊语 tornos（车床），本义为绕圈旋转，同族词有 return、turning、turnout。

sensesIntro.en: Motion round a centre first, then a change of direction, then a change of nature, and last the chance that comes round.
sensesIntro.cn: 先是绕心的转动，再是方向改变，再是性质改变，最后是绕回来的机会。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a hand turning a door handle.
core.cn: 核心意象：手拧门把。

branches.en: The pivot branch: one point stays still.
branches.cn: 支点分支：一个点不动。

branches.en: The direction branch: the body follows the hand.
branches.cn: 方向分支：身体跟着手转。

branches.en: The change branch: turning becomes becoming.
branches.cn: 变化分支：转变成「变成」。

branches.en: The order branch: turns go round and come back.
branches.cn: 次序分支：转圈后回到原处。

branches.en: The cycle branch: a handle and a rota both turn.
branches.cn: 循环分支：门把与值班表都在转。

intro.en: Turn is a free root from French, and its family grows through prefixes such as re- and over-.
intro.cn: turn 是来自法语自由词根，其词族靠 re-、over- 等前缀扩展。

latinIntro.en: Latin tornare, to turn, yields the whole family, listed below.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 tornare（转）生出整个词族，列在下面。

definition_zh: 二；两个
definition_en: the number that comes after one and before three
core_image: 两只一模一样的杯子并排立在窗台
scene: 清晨的巴士站，等车的人不多，只有两个。Two passengers stood at the bus stop in the rain.
sceneCN: 这里 two 是「二」（第 1 个义项：一之后、三之前的数目）；句意为雨中有两名乘客站在巴士站。两只杯子并排的画面，就是这个词的样子。

derivatives.zh: 与 two 同义的序数词，义为「第二」
由与 two 同源的词干构成，义为「两次；两倍」
由与 two 同源的词根构成，义为「双胞胎之一」
由 two 加复数词尾构成，义为「若干个二」

senses.title: The count of two
senses.definition: the number between one and three
senses.definitionCN: 介于一的与三之间的数目
senses.example: Two passengers stood at the bus stop in the rain.
senses.exampleCN: 雨中有两名乘客站在巴士站。
senses.why: The word is one of the oldest Germanic numbers and has changed very little.
senses.whyCN: 这个词是最古老的日耳曼数词之一，几乎没变过形。

senses.title: The pair
senses.definition: a group made up of that number, often a natural pair
senses.definitionCN: 由这个数组成的一组，常指天生的一对
senses.example: The shoes cost less if you take the two together.
senses.exampleCN: 两件一起买更便宜。
senses.why: A count used of natural pairs turns into the name of the pair itself.
senses.whyCN: 用来数天生成对之物的数词，转指这一对本身。

senses.title: The split in half
senses.definition: a division of one thing into that number of parts
senses.definitionCN: 把一样东西分成这个数目的份
senses.example: She cut the cake in two and gave him the larger half.
senses.exampleCN: 她把蛋糕切成两半，把大的那半给了他。
senses.why: To cut in two is to use the number as a way of dividing rather than counting.
senses.whyCN: 切成两半是用这个数划分事物，而非清点事物。

intro.en: Two belongs to the oldest layer of English and has close relatives in nearly every related language.
intro.cn: two 属于英语最古老的一层，几乎在所有亲属语言里都有对应的词。

items.en: The root twai named a pair in the earliest Germanic speech.
items.cn: 词根 twai 在最早的日耳曼语中命名成对之物。

items.en: Twa was used for men, and a neuter form for other things.
items.cn: twa 用于人，另有一个中性形式用于其他事物。

items.en: Two replaced the older forms and lost its final syllable.
items.cn: two 取代了旧形式，也丢掉了末音节。

items.en: The w is silent, but it shows up again in twice and twin.
items.cn: w 不发音，却在 twice 与 twin 里重新现形。

items.en: The word sits inside dozens of compounds, from twofold to twenty.
items.cn: 从 twofold 到 twenty，数十个合成词里都有它。

note.en: The first group holds words built on the same root, the second holds neighbouring numbers.
note.cn: 第一组是同根词，第二组是邻近的数词。

entries.definition: Two times.
One of a pair of children.
One of the digits of a foot.
Two things of a kind.
The number before two.
The number after two.

normalIntro.en: Two hides a w that never sounds but always returns in its relatives.
normalIntro.cn: two 藏着一个从不发音的 w，却在亲属词里常常回来。

normal.en: The w of two is silent, but spoken in twin and twice.
normal.cn: two 的 w 不发音，但在 twin、twice 里回来。

normal.en: In two means cut into halves.
normal.cn: in two 表示切成两半。

normal.en: Two by two means in pairs.
normal.cn: two by two 表示两个两个地。

normal.en: The ordinal of two is second, but second is shared with second in time.
normal.cn: two 的序数是 second，与「秒」同形。

normal.en: The tw- beginning marks hundreds of English words about pairing.
normal.cn: tw- 开头标记了成百个关于成对的英语词。

abstract.en: Two identical cups on a windowsill.
abstract.cn: 窗台上两只一模一样的杯子。

abstract.en: A line dividing a page into equal halves.
abstract.cn: 把一页纸对分的线。

abstract.en: Footprints, always in pairs.
abstract.cn: 总是成双的脚印。

examples.en: There are two ways to reach the station.
examples.cn: 去车站有两条路。

examples.en: The two of us walked home together.
examples.cn: 我们两个一起走回家。

examples.en: Cut the bread in two and share it.
examples.cn: 把面包切成两半，分着吃。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「兔」——兔子有两只长耳朵，正好两个。

root: 源自中古英语 two、古英语 twa/twa，属日耳曼语最古老的数词层，同族词有 twice、twin、twist、twenty。

sensesIntro.en: First the number, then a natural pair, then the act of splitting something into halves.
sensesIntro.cn: 先是数目，再是天生的一对，最后是把它当作划分的一半。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two equal cups side by side.
core.cn: 核心意象：并排的两只同样的杯子。

branches.en: The number branch: one step past one.
branches.cn: 数目分支：比一多一步。

branches.en: The pair branch: what goes together.
branches.cn: 成对分支：总在一起的两者。

branches.en: The half branch: one whole cut in two.
branches.cn: 一半分支：整体被分成两份。

branches.en: The counting branch: hundreds grow from twos.
branches.cn: 计数分支：成百由一个个二组成。

branches.en: The choice branch: only two sides exist.
branches.cn: 选择分支：只有两边可站。

intro.en: Two is a bare Germanic numeral, so its structure lies in the compounds it joins.
intro.cn: two 是光秃秃的日耳曼数词，它的结构藏在所入合成词里。

latinIntro.en: Latin duo gave English the duo- family, listed below.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 duo 为英语带来 duo- 词族，列在下面。

items.exampleCN: 它开头的 duo 与 duplex 都含二。
它开头的 twist 与 twenty 都含此意。

definition_zh: 类型；种类；打字；键入
definition_en: a class of things sharing features, or to write on a keyboard
core_image: 一排金属字模从盒子里被拣出来，按在纸上留下同一形状的印记
scene: 灯光下，一个人把要交的报告一行行敲进电脑。She typed the last line and saved the file.
sceneCN: 这里 type 是「打字；键入」（第 3 个义项：通过键盘逐个输入字符）；句意为她打完最后一行并保存了文件。指尖在键盘上逐个落下的动作，就是这个词的样子。

derivatives.zh: 由 type 加 -ical 构成，义为「典型的」
由 type 加 -ing 构成，义为「打字」
由 type 与 writer 合成，义为「打字机」
由 type 加 -ist 构成，义为「打字员」

senses.title: The family likeness
senses.definition: a group of things that share the same features
senses.definitionCN: 具有相同特征的一类事物
senses.example: This type of engine is common in small boats.
senses.exampleCN: 这种发动机在小船上很常见。
senses.why: The noun first named the shared form, the stamp that made many copies alike.
senses.whyCN: 名词起初指共有的形状，即许多复制品共用的那个印模。

senses.title: The metal letter
senses.definition: a small block of metal with a raised letter used for printing
senses.definitionCN: 印有凸起字母的金属小块，用于印刷
senses.example: The printer sorted the worn type back into its box.
senses.exampleCN: 印刷工把磨旧的活字重新装回字盒。
senses.why: A type was the physical thing that pressed a shape onto paper, the same word for the class and the stamp.
senses.whyCN: 活字正是把形状压到纸上的实物，同一个词兼指类别与印模。

senses.title: The tapping keys
senses.definition: to write by pressing keys on a machine or keyboard
senses.definitionCN: 通过按键在机器或键盘上书写
senses.example: She typed the last line and saved the file.
senses.exampleCN: 她打完最后一行并保存了文件。
senses.why: Since the letters came from type, the act of setting them became typing.
senses.whyCN: 因为字母来自活字，排印它们的动作便成了 typing。

intro.en: Type comes from Greek typos, a blow or the mark a blow leaves, through Latin and French.
intro.cn: type 来自希腊语 typos（一击、一击留下的印），经拉丁语与法语传下。

items.en: Typos meant a blow, and then the mark stamped by a blow.
items.cn: typos 意为击打，进而指击打留下的印痕。

items.en: Typus borrowed the idea of a figure or an image.
items.cn: typus 借来了图案、形象的意思。

items.en: French type narrowed it to a symbol or a model.
items.cn: 法语 type 把它收窄为符号或模型。

items.en: Printing gave it a body: movable type, a block that stamps letters.
items.cn: 印刷使它有了实体：活字，即压出字母的块。

items.en: From printing the word spread to kinds of things and to typing on keys.
items.cn: 从印刷扩展到事物的种类，再扩展到敲键盘。

note.en: The first group shares the Greek stem, the second names classes and keyboard work.
note.cn: 第一组共享希腊词干，第二组是类别与键盘操作相关词。

entries.definition: Showing the usual features.
A machine for typing.
A printing mistake.
A class of similar things.
A group in a system of classes.
The set of keys used to type.

normalIntro.en: Type began as a blow and ended as a keyboard: the mark and the making of marks.
normalIntro.cn: type 从一击开始，落到了键盘上：印痕与制造印痕。

normal.en: Type goes with typical, which means showing the type.
normal.cn: type 与 typical 同源，后者意为体现这一类的样子。

normal.en: Type of takes a singular type even before a plural noun.
normal.cn: type of 后用单数 type。

normal.en: Type in means to enter text on a screen.
normal.cn: type in 表示在屏幕上录入。

normal.en: Blood type shows how the word names a class.
normal.cn: blood type 显示它如何命名类别。

normal.en: Typing is not writing by hand, but both leave marks.
normal.cn: 打字不是手写，但都在留下痕迹。

abstract.en: A row of metal letters in a wooden tray.
abstract.cn: 木盘里一排金属字母。

abstract.en: A finger coming down on one key.
abstract.cn: 一根手指落在某个键上。

abstract.en: One shape stamped many times on one page.
abstract.cn: 同一个形状在纸页上被压了许多次。

examples.en: I typed my address into the form.
examples.cn: 我把地址输入了表格。

examples.en: That type of plant needs little water.
examples.cn: 那种植物几乎不需要水。

examples.en: She can type faster than she can write by hand.
examples.cn: 她打字比手写还快。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「太普」——太普通的一类，大家都属于同一种类型。

root: 源自晚期拉丁语 typus、希腊语 typos（一击、印痕），本义为压出的印记，进而指类别的模型，同族词有 typical、typewriter、typist、typo。

sensesIntro.en: First the class of things, then the metal block that prints them, then the act of pressing keys.
sensesIntro.cn: 先是事物的类别，再是印出字母的金属块，最后是敲键的动作。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a metal letter pressed on a page.
core.cn: 核心意象：压在纸上的金属活字。

branches.en: The class branch: many things share one stamp.
branches.cn: 类别分支：许多事物共一个印模。

branches.en: The print branch: the block behind the letter.
branches.cn: 印刷分支：字母背后的那块金属。

branches.en: The key branch: the stamping done by fingers.
branches.cn: 按键分支：用手指完成的压印。

branches.en: The trade branch: printers sort their types.
branches.cn: 行业分支：印刷工整理活字。

branches.en: The machine branch: stamps become keys.
branches.cn: 机器分支：印模变成按键。

intro.en: Type is a Greek root, and the family grows with -ical, -ist, -ing and compounds.
intro.cn: type 是希腊词根，词族靠 -ical、-ist、-ing 及合成扩展。

latinIntro.en: The Latin form typus supplied the whole family, listed below.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁形式 typus 供应了整个词族，列在下面。

definition_zh: 典型的；有代表性的；特有的
definition_en: showing the usual features of a group, or happening in the usual way
core_image: 一排相似的老房子，其中一栋可以代表整条街
scene: 海边小镇的早晨，渔船一条条回港，街上飘着鱼汤的味道。A typical morning here begins with the boats coming in.
sceneCN: 这里 typical 是「典型的；有代表性的」（第 1 个义项：体现某一类事物共性特征）；句意为这里典型的早晨从渔船回港开始。可以代表整条街的那栋老房子，就是这个词的画面。

derivatives.zh: 由 typical 加 -ly 构成，义为「典型地；通常」
由 typical 加 -ity 构成，义为「典型性」
由 typical 加前缀 a- 构成，义为「非典型的」

senses.title: The one that stands for all
senses.definition: having the features that most members of a group share
senses.definitionCN: 具有某一群体多数成员共有的特征
senses.example: A typical morning here begins with the boats coming in.
senses.exampleCN: 这里典型的早晨从渔船回港开始。
senses.why: The word points at a sample good enough to stand for the whole group.
senses.whyCN: 这个词指向一个足以代表整群的样本。

senses.title: The habit that marks you
senses.definition: showing the special character of a person or thing, often in a slightly critical way
senses.definitionCN: 显示某人某物特有的性格，常略带批评意味
senses.example: It was typical of him to arrive without calling.
senses.exampleCN: 不打电话就来，正是他一贯的作风。
senses.why: If a feature is shared by a group, it can also be the mark by which one member is known.
senses.whyCN: 若某特征是群体共有，也可成为辨认某个成员的特有标记。

intro.en: Typical is built on type plus the adjective ending -ical, and means of the stamp or the class.
intro.cn: typical 由 type 加形容词词尾 -ical 构成，意为「具有这一印模的」。

items.en: Typos named a blow and the mark left by it.
items.cn: typos 指一击以及它留下的印。

items.en: Typicus appeared in late Latin for something figurative.
items.cn: 晚期拉丁语 typicus 指具有图像或象征意味的东西。

items.en: The ending -ical joined type to make typical in the seventeenth century.
items.cn: 十七世纪 -ical 与 type 结合成 typical。

items.en: Science used it for a specimen that represents a whole species.
items.cn: 科学用它指代表整个物种的标本。

items.en: Everyday speech widened it to anything usual or characteristic.
items.cn: 日常语言把它扩展到一切寻常或有代表性的事物。

note.en: The first group shares the type stem, the second holds words of the same meaning.
note.cn: 第一组共享 type 词干，第二组是同义词。

entries.definition: In the usual manner.
Not usual for its group.
About current affairs.
Standing for a larger group.
Typical of a person or thing.
Happening most often.

normalIntro.en: Typical means of the type: the sample that wears the class face.
normalIntro.cn: typical 意为「属于这一类的」：长着这一类的脸的样本。

normal.en: Type plus -ical makes the adjective typical.
normal.cn: type 加 -ical 成形容词 typical。

normal.en: Typical of is the set phrase for a characteristic mark.
normal.cn: typical of 是表示「某物特有的」固定搭配。

normal.en: The a- in atypical means not.
normal.cn: atypical 里的 a- 表示「不」。

normal.en: Typically works as a sentence adverb: typically, it rained.
normal.cn: typically 常作句副词：typically, it rained。

normal.en: A typical example is chosen to speak for many.
normal.cn: 典型例子是被选来代表许多个的。

abstract.en: One plain house standing in a row of similar houses.
abstract.cn: 一排相似房屋中一栋普通的房子。

abstract.en: A sample jar labelled to represent a species.
abstract.cn: 标着物种名的标本瓶。

abstract.en: Rain arriving at the same hour every afternoon.
abstract.cn: 每天下午同一时刻到来的雨。

examples.en: This is a typical example of village architecture.
examples.cn: 这是乡村建筑的典型例子。

examples.en: It is typical of her to help without being asked.
examples.cn: 不用人求就帮忙，正是她的作风。

examples.en: Winter here is typical of the whole coast.
examples.cn: 这里的冬天代表了整个海岸一带。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「提皮扣」——提起皮包就能当代表的那一位，最典型。

root: 由 type（类型、印模，源自希腊语 typos 一击与印痕）加形容词词尾 -ical 构成，本义为具有该类特征的，同族词有 typically、typicality、atypical。

sensesIntro.en: First the sample that stands for its class, then the trait that marks an individual.
sensesIntro.cn: 先是能代表类别的样本，再是标记个体的特性。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one plain house that speaks for the row.
core.cn: 核心意象：一间足以代表整排的普通房子。

branches.en: The sample branch: one stands for many.
branches.cn: 样本分支：一个代表许多。

branches.en: The mark branch: the trait that names you.
branches.cn: 标记分支：能叫出你名字的特征。

branches.en: The ordinary branch: nothing unusual happens.
branches.cn: 寻常分支：没有特别的事发生。

branches.en: The judgement branch: typical can gently blame.
branches.cn: 评价分支：常带一点温和的抱怨。

branches.en: The science branch: a specimen defined by its type.
branches.cn: 科学分支：以模式标本定的物种。

intro.en: Typical is type plus -ical, and the family grows with -ly, -ity and the negative a-.
intro.cn: typical 是 type 加 -ical，词族靠 -ly、-ity 与否定前缀 a- 扩展。

latinIntro.en: The late Latin adjective typicus stands behind the English form, listed below.
latinIntro.cn: 英语形式背后是晚期拉丁语形容词 typicus，列在下面。

items.exampleCN: 它构成 typical 与 topical。

definition_zh: 丑陋的；难看的；丑恶的；险恶的；令人不快的
definition_en: unpleasant to look at, morally bad, or threatening in an unspecified way
core_image: 一张脸皱起来，让人本能地想转开眼睛
scene: 镜子前，孩子画的自画像把鼻子画得歪歪扭扭，他自己也忍不住捂住了嘴。The drawing was so ugly that the whole class burst out laughing.
sceneCN: 这里 ugly 是「难看的、丑陋的」（第 1 个义项：外表不悦目）；句意为那幅画难看得全班都笑出了声。皱起的一张脸让人想转开眼睛，正是这个词的核心画面。

collocations.zh: 丑小鸭；起初不起眼而后出众的人

derivatives.zh: 形容词加 -ness 构成名词，义为「丑陋；丑恶」
形容词加 -ify 构成动词，义为「使变丑」
复合形容词，义为「样子难看的」

senses.title: Unpleasant to look at
senses.definition: unpleasant or unattractive in appearance
senses.definitionCN: 外表上令人不快、不好看的
senses.example: An ugly stain spread across the white tablecloth.
senses.exampleCN: 一块难看的污渍在白桌布上漫开。
senses.why: The word comes from Old Norse uggligr, which carried a sense of something to be dreaded, and the visual sense grew out of that dread.
senses.whyCN: 这个词来自古诺斯语 uggligr，本带「令人畏惧」之意，视觉上的「难看」是从畏惧感里长出来的。

senses.title: Morally bad or shameful
senses.definition: morally offensive or shameful in a way that arouses disgust
senses.definitionCN: 道德上令人反感、使人厌恶的
senses.example: The trial exposed the ugly side of the business.
senses.exampleCN: 这场审讯暴露了这门生意丑恶的一面。
senses.why: From something dreadful to look at, the word easily moves to something dreadful to think about.
senses.whyCN: 从「看着可怕」很自然地滑到「想着可怕」，丑陋的外表就转成了丑陋的行为。

senses.title: Threatening or dangerous in an unclear way
senses.definition: used of a situation that looks threatening and may turn violent
senses.definitionCN: 用于形容看起来凶险、可能失控的局面
senses.example: The argument was starting to turn ugly.
senses.exampleCN: 争吵开始变得凶险起来。
senses.why: A scene that makes people wince is also a scene that may explode, so ugly marks rising tension.
senses.whyCN: 让人皱眉的场面往往也是随时会爆开的场面，于是 ugly 又用来标记气氛的紧张。

senses.title: Unpleasantly large or strong
senses.definition: used informally of an amount or problem that is unpleasantly big
senses.definitionCN: 非正式地形容数量或问题大得让人不舒服
senses.example: There is an ugly gap between the two reports.
senses.exampleCN: 两份报告之间有一道大得难看的鸿沟。
senses.why: Anything that makes you pull back your head can be called ugly, including an alarming figure.
senses.whyCN: 任何让你下意识缩头的东西都能叫 ugly，包括一个吓人的数字。

senses.title: Unattractive in a homely way
senses.definition: plain or ugly in appearance but not evil, often said of buildings or objects
senses.definitionCN: 外形朴素难看，但不含恶意，常用来形容建筑或器物
senses.example: They built an ugly block of flats by the river.
senses.exampleCN: 他们在河边盖了一栋难看的公寓楼。
senses.why: This is the neutral everyday use: nothing dreadful, only an eye that refuses to rest on the thing.
senses.whyCN: 这是最中性的日常用法：并不可怕，只是眼睛不愿在它上面停留。

intro.en: The adjective is Scandinavian in origin and entered English in the Middle Ages.
intro.cn: 这个形容词源于斯堪的纳维亚语，中世纪进入英语。

items.en: Uggligr meant dreadful or to be feared, built on a root meaning fear.
items.cn: uggligr 意为「可怕的、令人畏惧的」，其词根表示恐惧。

items.en: The suffix -ligr corresponds to English -ly, so the word first described a manner rather than a face.
items.cn: 后缀 -ligr 相当于英语 -ly，因此这个词最早形容的是一种样子，而非一张脸。

items.en: English borrowed the word in the northern forms as ugly, still with the sense of fearful.
items.cn: 英语以北方方言形式借入作 ugly，仍保留「可怕」之义。

items.en: By the seventeenth century the sense of frightening had faded and appearance took over.
items.cn: 到十七世纪，「令人恐惧」的意味淡去，外观义占了上风。

items.en: Later centuries extend it to behaviour, situations, and amounts.
items.cn: 此后的几个世纪里，它又扩展到行为、局势与数量。

note.en: The look-alike group collects other -ly words, and the near-meaning group gathers adjectives of appearance.
note.cn: 形近组收集其他以 -ly 收尾的形容词，近义组汇集表示外观的其他形容词。

entries.definition: the quality of being ugly
very much, to a great degree
entries.definitionCN: 极其；非常（只是拼写相近，词源不同）

entries.definition: with strong interest
entries.definitionCN: 热切地（只是拼写相近，词源不同）

entries.definition: extremely ugly or unpleasant
not beautiful or decorated
not pleasing in appearance
entries.definitionCN: 不好看的；没有吸引力的

entries.definition: very pleasing to look at

normalIntro.en: The word began as a label for what makes people afraid, and the sense slid from dread to looks.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词起初标记让人害怕之物，意义由畏惧滑向外观。

normal.en: Ugly and dread share a northern origin, so a fearful shape becomes a bad-looking one.
normal.cn: ugly 与「畏惧」同出北方语言，可怕的样子就变成了难看的样子。

normal.en: Turn ugly is the phrase where the old fear still shows: the mood becomes dangerous.
normal.cn: turn ugly 这个搭配里还能看见旧日的恐惧：气氛变得危险。

normal.en: Ugly duckling comes from Andersen and means someone plain who grows remarkable.
normal.cn: ugly duckling 出自安徒生，指起初平平而后出众的人。

normal.en: Ugliness is the noun, uglify the verb that means to make ugly.
normal.cn: ugliness 是名词，uglify 是使变丑的动词。

normal.en: Uglier and ugliest double the final consonant before -er and -est.
normal.cn: 比较级 uglier 与最高级 ugliest 都在 -er 与 -est 前把 g 双写。

abstract.en: Picture a face in a funhouse mirror, features pulled sideways.
abstract.cn: 想象哈哈镜里的一张脸，五官被拉向一边。

abstract.en: Hear the crowd turn from laughter to a hard silence.
abstract.cn: 听人群从笑声转为僵硬的沉默。

abstract.en: Then feel the same discomfort when a number on a report is too large.
abstract.cn: 再把同样的不适感挪到一个报表上过大的数字。

examples.en: That building is the ugliest one on the street.
examples.cn: 那栋楼是街上最难看的一栋。

examples.en: The mood in the room turned ugly after the vote.
examples.cn: 投票之后屋里的气氛变得凶险。

examples.en: She refused to believe that an ugly past decides a bright future.
examples.cn: 她不肯相信一段丑恶的过去会决定一个光明的未来。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「阿格丽」——阿格丽小姐一皱眉，整张脸就垮得让人不敢看。

root: 古诺斯语 uggligr（可怕的、可畏的），词根表示「恐惧」，后缀 -ligr 相当于英语 -ly；中古英语北方方言借入作 ugly

sensesIntro.en: One core feeling, unease at what meets the eye, spreads from faces to deeds, moods, and figures.
sensesIntro.cn: 一份核心感受，眼睛见到时的不适，由面孔蔓延到行为、气氛与数字。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a face that makes you want to look away.
core.cn: 核心意象：一张让人想转开眼睛的脸。

branches.en: The visual branch: faces, buildings, and objects that the eye rejects.
branches.cn: 视觉分支：眼睛拒绝停留的脸、建筑与器物。

branches.en: The moral branch, where a deed is as hard to look at as a scar.
branches.cn: 道德分支：一桩行为像伤疤一样让人不敢看。

branches.en: The mood branch, where a scene threatens to break open.
branches.cn: 气氛分支：场面随时可能炸开。

branches.en: The quantity branch, where a figure is unpleasantly large.
branches.cn: 数量分支：一个数字大得让人不适。

branches.en: The plain descriptive sense that most learners meet first.
branches.cn: 最朴素的描写义，也是学习者最先遇到的义项。

intro.en: The word is not built from Latin parts but from a northern suffix attached to a stem of fear.
intro.cn: 这个词不由拉丁部件构成，而是恐惧词干加北方语言后缀。

latinIntro.en: There is no Latin ancestor here, so the Latin list is left empty.
latinIntro.cn: 此词没有拉丁语祖先，故拉丁同源词一栏留空。

items.example: Ugly once named what people feared.
items.exampleCN: ugly 曾经指人们畏惧的东西。

items.example: Ugly and lonely both end in -ly as adjectives.
items.exampleCN: ugly 与 lonely 都以 -ly 收尾而作形容词。

items.example: They uglified the square with billboards.
items.exampleCN: 他们用广告牌把广场弄得很难看。

items.example: The ugliness of the plan shocked them.
items.exampleCN: 计划的丑恶让他们震惊。

definition_zh: 叔叔；伯伯；舅舅；姑父；姨父；（口语）大叔
definition_en: the brother of one’s father or mother, or the husband of an aunt
core_image: 饭桌旁那位总爱给你夹菜、跟父母同辈的男子
scene: 过年时家里人挤满一张大圆桌，坐在孩子旁边的那位笑眯眯地往他碗里添了一块鱼。My uncle taught me how to ride a bicycle.
sceneCN: 这里 uncle 是「舅舅或叔叔」（第 1 个义项：父或母的兄弟）；句意为叔叔教会了我骑自行车。饭桌旁给你夹菜的那位长辈正是这个词的画面。

collocations.zh: 汤姆叔叔（亦指谄媚白人者）

derivatives.zh: 对应词，义为「姑妈；姨妈；婶婶」
源自拉丁语同义词，义为「像叔伯般慈爱的」
复合名词，义为「叔伯关系的姻亲」

senses.title: Brother of one’s parent
senses.definition: the brother of your mother or your father
senses.definitionCN: 父亲或母亲的兄弟
senses.example: My uncle lives in the next town.
senses.exampleCN: 我叔叔住在邻镇。
senses.why: The word comes from Latin avunculus, a mother’s brother, which is itself a diminutive of avus, grandfather.
senses.whyCN: 这个词来自拉丁语 avunculus（舅父），而 avunculus 本身是 avus（祖父）的指小形式。

senses.title: Husband of one’s aunt
senses.definition: the husband of your aunt, without blood relation
senses.definitionCN: 姑妈或姨妈的丈夫，与其无血缘关系
senses.example: Her uncle drove us to the station.
senses.exampleCN: 她姨父开车送我们去车站。
senses.why: Once a term marks a position at the family table, it covers whoever sits there by marriage.
senses.whyCN: 一旦一个词标记的是家庭餐桌上的位置，坐在那里的人无论因何而来都会被它覆盖。

senses.title: An older man addressed informally
senses.definition: a friendly form of address to a much older man
senses.definitionCN: 对年长许多的男子表示亲近的称呼
senses.example: The uncle at the night stall sold us warm buns.
senses.exampleCN: 夜市摊上的大叔卖给我们热包子。
senses.why: A family kinship word stretches into a polite warmth for strangers of the older generation.
senses.whyCN: 亲族称谓延伸到对陌生长辈的一种亲切礼貌。

senses.title: A relative of an earlier generation more generally
senses.definition: any male relative of your parents’ generation in a wide family
senses.definitionCN: 大家族中父母一辈的男性亲长
senses.example: In that village every older man is called uncle.
senses.exampleCN: 在那个村子里，年长的男人都被叫作叔叔。
senses.why: Kin terms spread outward along the ring of the family until the whole generation is covered.
senses.whyCN: 亲族称谓沿着家族的圆圈向外铺开，直到覆满整个辈分。

senses.title: Used in slang for surrender
senses.definition: in North American speech, to admit defeat by saying the word
senses.definitionCN: 在北美口语中，说一声 uncle 表示认输
senses.example: The small boy twisted away and cried uncle.
senses.exampleCN: 小男孩挣脱开，喊了声「服了」。
senses.why: A familiar name used under pressure turns into a signal of giving up.
senses.whyCN: 一个亲昵的称呼在受压制时，被转成投降的信号。

intro.en: The word goes back through French to a Latin diminutive of grandfather.
intro.cn: 这个词经法语上溯到拉丁语中「祖父」的指小形式。

items.en: Avus means grandfather, and avunculus is a little grandfather, that is the mother’s brother.
items.cn: avus 意为祖父，avunculus 就是「小祖父」，即舅父。

items.en: Old French oncle shortens and reshapes the Latin word.
items.cn: 古法语 oncle 把拉丁词缩短并改了形。

items.en: English borrows uncle around the thirteenth century.
items.cn: 英语在十三世纪前后借入 uncle。

items.en: The sense widens to cover the husband of an aunt and then older men in general.
items.cn: 词义扩大到姑父、姨父，进而泛指年长男子。

items.en: The North American idiom say uncle keeps the word inside children’s games.
items.cn: 北美习语 say uncle 让这个词留在儿童游戏里。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers kin words that look and sound similar, and the near-meaning group collects family terms.
note.cn: 形近组收集形音相近的亲属词，近义组收集家庭称谓。

entries.definition: a corner or a way of looking at something
entries.definitionCN: 角；角度（只是拼写相近，词源不同）

entries.definition: the joint between the leg and the foot
entries.definitionCN: 脚踝（只是拼写相近，词源不同）

entries.definition: kindly like an uncle
the sister of a parent
the son of your brother or sister
the child of your aunt or uncle
a mother or father

normalIntro.en: The Latin original means little grandfather, which explains why the word feels old and fond at once.
normalIntro.cn: 拉丁原词意为「小祖父」，这解释了它为什么既显年长又带亲昵。

normal.en: Avunculus was the mother’s brother, the little grandfather of a household.
normal.cn: avunculus 是舅父，家里的「小祖父」。

normal.en: Aunt is the matching word on the female side, and the pair are learned together.
normal.cn: aunt 是与之配套的阴性词，两个词常一起记。

normal.en: Avuncular is the adjective for an uncle-like manner, gentle and slightly teasing.
normal.cn: avuncular 是形容叔伯作风的形容词，温和又略带打趣。

normal.en: Say uncle is the North American signal of surrender in a wrestle.
normal.cn: say uncle 是北美口语里角力时认输的信号。

normal.en: The plural is regular: uncles, with no change of the stem.
normal.cn: 复数规则变化作 uncles，词干不变。

abstract.en: See a round dinner table with one man leaning to fill a child’s bowl.
abstract.cn: 看见一张圆饭桌，一位男子俯身为孩子添饭。

abstract.en: Hear your own childhood name called by a voice one generation lower.
abstract.cn: 听见比你高一辈的声音喊你的小名。

abstract.en: Then pass the same warmth to an older stranger at a night stall.
abstract.cn: 再把同样的亲切递给夜市摊上一位年长陌生人。

examples.en: My uncle fixed the leak in the roof last Sunday.
examples.cn: 上星期天我叔叔修好了屋顶的漏水。

examples.en: She has three uncles on her mother’s side.
examples.cn: 她母亲那边有三个舅舅。

examples.en: The two brothers wrestled until the smaller one said uncle.
examples.cn: 两兄弟扭打了很久，直到小的那个喊了声服了。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「安口」——叔叔一进门就先安顿好你的嘴，总往你嘴里塞吃的。

root: 拉丁语 avus（祖父）的指小形式 avunculus（舅父），经古法语 oncle 进入英语；同族有 aunt、avuncular

sensesIntro.en: The word starts as the mother’s brother and widens along the family’s older generation until any warm older man can be called it.
sensesIntro.cn: 这个词从舅父开始，沿家族的上一个辈分不断扩大，直到任何亲切的年长男子都能用它。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: the man beside the child at the family table.
core.cn: 核心意象：家庭餐桌旁坐在孩子身边的那位男子。

branches.en: The blood branch: brothers of either parent.
branches.cn: 血缘分支：父母双方的兄弟。

branches.en: The marriage branch, where an aunt’s husband joins in.
branches.cn: 婚姻分支：姑父、姨父被纳入。

branches.en: The widened branch: any older man of the parents’ generation.
branches.cn: 扩展分支：父母一辈的任何年长男子。

definition_zh: 在……下面；在……之下；少于
definition_en: in or to a position below something, or below a stated amount
core_image: 一张桌子下面缩着一只躲雨的猫
scene: 雷雨忽至，院子里的人跑进屋，猫却钻进了桌底。The cat slept under the table all afternoon.
sceneCN: 这里 under 是「在……下面」（第 1 个义项：处在某物的下方）；句意为那只猫一下午都睡在桌子下面。桌底下缩着猫的画面，就是这个词的样子。

derivatives.zh: 由 under 加古词尾构成，义为「在……下面」
由 under 与 ground 合成，义为「地下的」
由 under 与 stand 合成，义为「理解」
由 under 与 way 合成，义为「进行中的」

senses.title: Beneath the table
senses.definition: in a position lower than and often covered by something
senses.definitionCN: 处于比某物更低、常被其遮住的位置
senses.example: The cat slept under the table all afternoon.
senses.exampleCN: 那只猫一下午都睡在桌子下面。
senses.why: The oldest sense is simply lower and covered, with something above you.
senses.whyCN: 最古老的意思就是位置更低且被遮住，头顶上还有东西。

senses.title: Below the mark
senses.definition: less than a particular number, age or level
senses.definitionCN: 少于某个数目、年龄或水平
senses.example: Children under twelve travel free.
senses.exampleCN: 十二岁以下儿童免费乘车。
senses.why: Below in space becomes below in amount: the same picture done to a scale.
senses.whyCN: 空间里的「在下」变成数量上的「不到」：同一个图景用在刻度上。

senses.title: Beneath the weight
senses.definition: while being affected by a condition, rule or authority
senses.definitionCN: 处于某种条件、规则或权力的作用之中
senses.example: The bridge is still under repair.
senses.exampleCN: 这座桥仍在维修中。
senses.why: Whatever presses down on you from above holds you in its state, so under also marks conditions.
senses.whyCN: 凡从上方压下来的东西都使你处在其状态里，于是 under 也标记处境。

senses.title: Sinking below
senses.definition: in or into a lower position, used without an object
senses.definitionCN: 处于或进入更低的位置，不带宾语
senses.example: The boat went under within minutes.
senses.exampleCN: 船几分钟内就沉了下去。
senses.why: When the object is obvious, the preposition stands alone as an adverb.
senses.whyCN: 当所及之物不言自明时，介词便独自作副词用。

intro.en: Under is a very old Germanic word built on a root that meant beneath or among.
intro.cn: under 是极古老的日耳曼词，词根源意为「在下」或「在其中」。

items.en: The root carried the sense of being lower or in the middle of a group.
items.cn: 词根表达位于更低处或处在群体中间。

items.en: Under worked as preposition and adverb from the earliest texts.
items.cn: under 从最早的文本起就兼作介词与副词。

items.en: It also meant under the rule of someone, as under a king.
items.cn: 它也表示受某人统治，如 under a king。

items.en: The form has changed almost nothing in a thousand years.
items.cn: 一千年来这个词形几乎没变。

items.en: English used it to build hundreds of compounds, from understand to underground.
items.cn: 英语用它造出数百个合成词，从 understand 到 underground。

note.en: The first group shares the old root, the second holds prepositions of position.
note.cn: 第一组共享古老词根，第二组是方位介词。

normalIntro.en: Under is the plain word for having something above your head.
normalIntro.cn: under 就是「头顶之上有东西」的朴素说法。

normal.en: Under pairs with over; below pairs with above.
normal.cn: under 与 over 相对，below 与 above 相对。

normal.en: Below often uses a scale, under often uses a cover.
normal.cn: below 常用于刻度，under 常用于遮盖。

normal.en: Under can mean less than: under ten minutes.
normal.cn: under 可表不足：under ten minutes。

normal.en: Dozens of compounds begin with under-.
normal.cn: 大量合成词以 under- 开头。

normal.en: American speech shortens the last vowel to a light er.
normal.cn: 美式口语末元音弱读。

abstract.cn: 一只缩在桌腿下的猫。

abstract.cn: 一只手把船按到水面以下。

abstract.en: A roof slanting over a doorway.
abstract.cn: 斜在门口上方的屋檐。

examples.cn: 他在坐垫下面找到了钥匙。

examples.en: The project is still under discussion.
examples.cn: 这个项目仍在讨论之中。

examples.en: Tickets cost under twenty pounds.
examples.cn: 票价不到二十英镑。

root: 源自中古英语 under、古英语 under，属日耳曼语最古老的方位词，本义为在下方或被遮住，同族词有 underneath、underground、understand。

sensesIntro.en: First below and covered, then below on a scale, then held under a condition, and finally standing alone.
sensesIntro.cn: 先是被遮在下，再是刻度之下，再是受制于某种处境，最后独立成副词。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a cat beneath a table.
core.cn: 核心意象：桌下的一只猫。

branches.en: The space branch: something above you.
branches.cn: 空间分支：上方有东西。

branches.en: The scale branch: below a number.
branches.cn: 刻度分支：低于某个数。

branches.en: The rule branch: pressed by a condition.
branches.cn: 条件分支：被某种处境压着。

branches.en: The verbless branch: the object drops away.
branches.cn: 独立分支：宾语省略了。

branches.en: The weight branch: cover becomes control.
branches.cn: 压力分支：遮盖变成支配。

intro.cn: under 是自由词，也作前缀出现在数百个合成词中。
